title: Quantum Boomerang Effect in Time-Crystalline Structures
authors: Qi-wen Peng, Krzysztof Sacha, Chu-hui Fan
abstract: The quantum boomerang effect (QBE) is a unique dynamical signature of Anderson localization, characterized by a launched wavepacket that initially drifts but ultimately returns to its initial position due to fundamental quantum interference. In this work, we theoretically establish and quantitatively characterize the QBE in a time-crystalline structure using a periodically driven quantum particle in a one-dimensional potential well. By constructing maximally localized Floquet-Wannier states and introducing temporal disorder, we rigorously map the continuous Floquet dynamics onto a discrete disordered tight-binding lattice. By positioning a detector at a fixed spatial coordinate, we monitor the temporal evolution of the wavepacket, to extract the mean temporal center of mass of the probability density in a time-crystalline structure. This mean temporal center of mass exhibits an initial ballistic expansion, followed by a pronounced U-turn, and ultimately returns to its initial temporal position after long-time evolution. These results confirm the existence of the complete QBE in the time domain. They also demonstrate that non-trivial dynamics can be explored within time-crystalline systems, even though these structures already possess an inherent temporal periodicity.
summary: The authors theoretically prove the existence of the Quantum Boomerang Effect in time-crystalline structures by analyzing wavepacket dynamics. They map the complex Floquet evolution onto a disordered tight-binding model, showing that temporal disorder causes the probability density to initially drift but ultimately return to its starting point. This demonstrates that disorder can stabilize quantum coherence in periodically driven systems.
main_problem: To theoretically establish and quantitatively characterize the Quantum Boomerang Effect (QBE) entirely within the time domain using a periodically driven system.
main_result: The QBE is confirmed in the time domain, showing that temporal disorder can induce a counterintuitive 'drift-and-return' behavior, stabilizing the mean arrival time through mechanisms analogous to Anderson localization.
method: The continuous Floquet dynamics are mapped onto a discrete disordered tight-binding lattice using maximally localized Floquet-Wannier states and analyzed via secular approximation techniques.
model_or_system: A quantum particle in a 1D potential well subjected to periodic time driving, modeled by an effective Hamiltonian that incorporates temporal disorder ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Mean temporal center of mass of the probability density $\langle	au(N)angle$, and the maximum temporal shift $\Delta	au_{	ext{max}}$.
important_parameters: The ratio of hopping strength to disorder strength ($J/\gamma$), and the resonance condition ($\omega = s\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The secular approximation is used to derive effective Hamiltonians, which are local descriptions valid near specific resonances.
figures_summary: Figures compare phase-space portraits (Fig. 1) and show probability densities $P_N(	au)$ demonstrating the drift and return behavior over time steps (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the QBE in a general Floquet context, deriving effective Hamiltonians via secular approximation, mapping to a disordered tight-binding model, and finally analyzing the role of disorder strength ($\gamma$) on the temporal dynamics.
why_interesting: This work connects concepts from Anderson localization (a hallmark of disorder) to time-periodic systems (time crystals), providing a novel mechanism for understanding coherence revival in driven quantum matter.
